head: faltar
gloss: to be left, to go (faltan diez minutos = ten minutes to go)

head: al revés
gloss: upside down; the wrong way round

head: gustar
gloss: to like (me gusta / no le gustan / nos gustan)

head: torta
gloss: cake (in Colombia and much of Latin America)

head: ayudar
gloss: to help (¿Me puede ayudar? = Can you help me?)

head: gente
gloss: people (singular in Spanish: hay mucha gente)

head: sin
gloss: without (sin + infinitive: sin mirar = without looking)

head: tía
gloss: aunt; el tío = uncle (los tíos = aunts and uncles)

head: gandules
gloss: pigeon peas (arroz con gandules = Puerto Rico's classic rice dish)

head: bizcocho
gloss: cake (Puerto Rico; party or wedding cake)

head: padrino
gloss: best man, wedding sponsor; also godfather

head: novios
gloss: the bride and groom; el novio = groom, boyfriend

head: guía
gloss: guide (a woman; a man is el guía; also 'guidebook')

head: siglo
gloss: century (el siglo quince = the 15th century, the 1400s)

head: llama
gloss: llama (the animal); careful: se llama = is called

head: quechua
gloss: Quechua (the language of the Incas, still spoken in Peru)

head: levantarse
gloss: to get up (se levanta = gets up)

head: sentarse
gloss: to sit down (se sienta = sits down)

head: moverse
gloss: to move (no se mueve = doesn't move)

head: torre del reloj
gloss: the Clock Tower (main gate of Cartagena's old city)

head: cocada
gloss: cocada (coconut sweet from Colombia's Caribbean coast)

head: subir
gloss: to get on, to go up

head: faltar
gloss: to be missing (falta algo = something is missing)

head: penalti
gloss: penalty kick (in Colombia people usually say el penal)

head: bombilla
gloss: light bulb (in Chile people say la ampolleta; there, a bombilla is the metal straw for mate)

head: ven
gloss: come! (in Buenos Aires people say vení; also tocá, tomá)

head: arrancar
gloss: to tear off, to pull off

head: encargarse de
gloss: to take care of, to make sure to

head: vos
gloss: you (informal, Uruguay and Argentina: vos venís = tú vienes)

head: chivito
gloss: Uruguayan steak sandwich; literally, a young goat (kid)

head: limitarse a
gloss: to just, to limit oneself to

head: mija
gloss: dear, sweetie (from mi hija; Mexico/Latin America)

head: acariciar
gloss: to stroke, to run one's hand over

head: alfombra
gloss: (here) street carpet made for a Holy Week procession

head: reverso
gloss: the back (of a photo or card)

head: rellenitos
gloss: sweet plantain dumplings filled with black beans (Guatemala)

head: descolgar
gloss: to take down (from a wall or hook)

head: cucurucho
gloss: robed procession bearer in Guatemala's Holy Week

head: postrado
gloss: laid up, confined (by illness or injury)

head: compostela
gloss: certificate given to pilgrims who complete the Camino

head: mojón
gloss: stone waymarker (with the distance to Santiago)

head: pulpo a feira
gloss: Galician-style octopus (boiled, with paprika and olive oil)

head: hospitalero
gloss: host who runs a pilgrims' hostel (often a volunteer)

head: jubileo
gloss: jubilee (special pardon granted in a Holy Year)

head: nena
gloss: sweetheart, dear (Arg., affectionate; lit. little girl)

head: advertir
gloss: to warn; to notice, point out

head: áncora
gloss: pallet fork (watch escapement part; lit. anchor)

head: comal
gloss: flat griddle (for tortillas and toasting chiles)

head: dirigirse la palabra
gloss: to speak to each other, be on speaking terms

head: molino
gloss: mill (here: a shop that grinds chiles, corn, etc.)

head: brotar
gloss: to spring forth, to pour out

head: minutero
gloss: street photographer with a box camera (Cuba)
